translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my beloved son: grace and mercy and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to God, whom I have served from the beginning with a pure mind, as I unceasingly remember you in my prayers night and day,
and I long to see you (I remember those tears of yours) so that I may be filled with joy.
I have called to mind the unfeigned faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your mother's mother Eunice; and I believe that it will dwell in you also.
For this reason I remind you to fan into fervent flame the grace of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God has not given us a spirit of fearfulness, but of power and of love and of purity.
So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, his prisoner. Instead, share in the suffering for the gospel by the power of God,
who saved us and called us with that holy calling, not because of our works but by his own will and grace, which was given to us through Christ Jesus before eternal times,
and which has now been revealed through the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who abolished death and brought life and incorruption to light through the gospel,
for which I have been appointed a preacher, an apostle and a teacher of the Gentiles.
For this reason I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed. For I know whom I have believed, and I believe that he is able to guard what I have entrusted to him until that coming day.
Keep as a pattern the healthy words that you heard from me, in the faith and love of Christ Jesus.
Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit, who has made his dwelling in us.
You know this: all who are in Asia have abandoned me, among them Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chains;
rather, when he came to Rome, he searched for me eagerly and found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And you know better than anyone how much he served me in Ephesus.
As for you, my son, be strong in the grace of Jesus Christ,
and what you heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust this to faithful people who will be able to teach others as well.
Endure hardship as a good fighter of Christ Jesus.
No fighter gets entangled in worldly affairs, so that he may please his commander.
If anyone is a fighter, he is not crowned unless he fights according to the rules.
The farmer who does the labour ought to be the first to receive a share of the fruit.
Think about what I am telling you, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the seed of David, according to my gospel,
for which I suffer hardship, even to the point of chains, as an evildoer; but the word of God is not bound.
For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may find life through Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
The saying is trustworthy: if we die with him, we shall also live with him.
If we endure, we shall reign with him; if we deny him, he too will deny us.
If we do not believe, he remains faithful; he cannot deny himself.
Remind them of these things before God, and charge them not to quarrel over words, which is of no use and only ruins those who hear.
Make every effort to present yourself before God as approved, a worker with no need to be ashamed, making progress in the word of truth.
But keep away from profane, empty talk, for those who engage in it will advance further into ungodliness,
and their talk will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
who have sinned against the truth by saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and they are overturning the faith of some.
But God's firm foundation stands, and it bears this seal: "The Lord knows those who are his," and: "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from falsehood."
In a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver but also of wood and of clay, some for honor and some for dishonor.
If anyone cleanses himself from all of this, he will be a vessel for honor, holy and useful to the Lord, prepared for every good work.
Flee youthful desires, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the name of the Lord from a pure heart.
But keep away from foolish and ignorant inquiries, knowing that they breed quarrels.
A servant of the Lord must not quarrel, but must be kind to all, able to teach, not resentful,
gently instructing those who oppose him, in case God may grant them repentance leading to knowledge of the truth,
and they may escape from the snare of the devil, by whom they have been captured to do his will.
But know this: in the last days evil times will come.
People will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to father and mother, ungrateful, unworthy, unloving,
implacable, slanderers, without self-control, unpeaceable, haters of good,
betrayers of their own households, reckless, puffed up, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God.
They will wear the outward form of godliness but deny its power. Keep away from such people.
For among them are those who creep into houses and take captive women who are weighed down with sins and who acquire many desires,
They are always learning and are never able to come to knowledge of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth: men corrupt in mind and untested in faith.
But they will not get any further, for their mind will be made plain to everyone, as theirs was too.
But you have followed my teaching, my way of life, my zeal, faith, long-suffering, love, and patience,
and the persecutions and sufferings that came upon me in Antioch, Iconium and Lystra. I endured so many persecutions, and the Lord delivered me from them all.
And all who wish to live in the service of God through Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
But wicked men and sorcerers will go on to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
But you, stand firm in what you have learned and believed, knowing from whom you learned it;
and that from childhood you have known the divine Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is of the Spirit of God and useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
so that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
I solemnly charge you before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom:
preach the word; keep at it in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke and encourage with all long-suffering and teaching.
For the time will come when they will not put up with the teaching of this life, but according to their own desires they will gather teaching for themselves with itching ears;
and they will turn their hearing away from the truth and turn to fables.
But you, be watchful in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and carry out your ministry well.
For I am now being offered up, and the time of my departure has come.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
From now on the crown of righteousness awaits me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day; and not only to me, but to all who have loved his appearing.
Hurry to come to me soon,
for Demas has left me, having loved this world, and has gone to Thessalonica; Crispus has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me.
Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me in the ministry.
I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the cloak that I left in Troas with Carpus, and the books as well, above all the parchments.
Alexander the smith did me much harm. May the Lord repay him according to his deeds.
You too beware of him, for he strongly opposed our words.
At my first defense no one stood with me, but all abandoned me. May it not be counted against them.
But the Lord stood with me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching might be fulfilled and all the Gentiles might hear it; and I was rescued from the mouth of the lion.
The Lord will deliver me from every evil deed and will save me into his heavenly kingdom. To him be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth; Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.
Hurry to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, as do Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers.
The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with us. Amen.
